pages.text: A specimen copies itself at a rate β; the ward clears it at its natural rate γ = 0.4 per day plus the quarantine field's own rate q. Each anomalous unit then makes R = β/(γ + q) more before it is cleared. Below 1 the specimen is contained and can be studied; the faster it grows the more there is to study - but at R above 1 it spreads through the containment. Clamp the field too hard and the specimen goes dormant and there is nothing to learn.
$(thing)Set$(): Growth rate β, Quarantine rate q.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The specimen's growth rate wanders by ±10%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): R above 1: the anomaly is spreading through the containment; The quarantine is so strong the specimen has gone dormant: nothing to study; The quarantine field is overheating the ward.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A faster-growing specimen held just below R = 1 gives the most to study.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective growth rate: β_eff = β·(1 + 0.1·d)$(br)Reproduction number R: R = β/(γ + q)$(br)Observable activity: A = β·R
